text: Toronto and Region Conservation Authority has designed an Indigenous outdoor gathering space co-developed with the Williams Treaty First Nation communities and with input from the City of Toronto. Known as Station 1 of the Morningside Legacy Project, the gathering space will be located west of Morningside Avenue and south of Ellesmere Road, on lands under the management of Parks and Recreation. Station 1 is an introductory space, welcoming visitors, and providing a seating area centered around a feature granite boulder that highlights treaty history. The Morningside Legacy Project seeks to acknowledge and honour the longtime presence of First Nations Peoples in the Morningside Park area through the creation of an outdoor gathering space that can be used for shared learning experiences and celebration. City Council on March 26 and 27, 2025, adopted the following: 1. City Council authorize the General Manager, Parks and Recreation, to accept a donation of up to $0.500 million from Toronto and Region Conservation Authority for the purposes of installing an Indigenous outdoor gathering space at Morningside Park, in compliance with the Donations to the City of Toronto for Community Benefits Policy. 2.
